item.title: Sunday Morning, Oct 18
item.description:
The Sunday morning bulletin from Gumshoe News Radio for October 18, 2026: Reuters reports President Trump is blaming aides as Republican midterm hopes dim, the A.P. tallies what the Iran war is costing households, a deadly explosion and fire at Canada's Wainwright military base, Ukraine's thousand-drone strike on St. Petersburg, Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the morning after France's riots, the fight over A.I. pricing in stores, OpenAI's free plan for university labs and new ChatGPT voices, a huge California student data breach and Florida's driver database notices, your X feed with Taylor Swift and a fruit fly in a virtual world, the Walk to End Alzheimer's and early voting in Andover, and a Rhode Island grower's record three-thousand-pound pumpkin. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

AAA and EIA figures via AP; Fortune on Moody's Mark Zandi estimate (Oct 17) - Global News, "7 dead, dozens injured in explosion and fire at CFB Wainwright" (Karen Bartko, updated Oct 18); AP via NPR, "Major fire breaks out in Alberta after deadly incident at military base" (Oct 18); National Defence Canada statement (Oct 17); AP, "Blaze at St Petersburg oil sites as Kyiv launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia" (Oct 18); Al Jazeera with AFP and Reuters (Oct 18); Kyiv Independent (Oct 18); Investing.com, "Tankers hit near Hormuz as Tehran offers U.S. reopening plan" (Oct 18); Reuters via Arab News (Oct 18); RTÉ with AFP, "Over 1,800 arrested amid clashes, looting during French protests" (Oct 18); The Times of Israel (Zev Stub, Oct 18) - AP, "Consumer apprehension grows as US retailers adopt AI-assisted pricing tools" (Dee-Ann Durbin and Anne D'Innocenzio, Oct 18) - OpenAI, "Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs" (Oct 15); OpenAI Help Center, ChatGPT release notes; Notebookcheck, "ChatGPT Voice: GPT-Live-1.1 brings new voices for six languages" - Los Angeles Times, "Hackers steal personal data of millions of California students in massive breach" (Howard Blume, Andrew Khouri and Jaweed Kaleem, Oct 16); The Florida Press, citing Florida Politics and FLHSMV (Oct 17) - Harry's X home timeline Oct 17 ~11:50 PM to Oct 18 ~6:55 AM ET (@Variety, @pmarca, @kimmonismus); Odyssey (@odysseyml) post, Oct 17, via Digg - Town of Andover, "Traffic Advisory: Downtown Andover Events This Weekend" (Oct 16); Andover News, "Early Voting Begins Saturday In Andover" (Dave Copeland, Oct 17) and "Murray, Shepley To Meet In Forum In Andover Oct. 20" (Oct 14); Town of Andover calendar, Howl-O-Ween (Oct 24) - Guinness World Records, "Pumpkinpalooza!: how the world's biggest pumpkin record fell twice in one week" (Adam Millward, Oct 14); WPRI, "Guinness verifies Rhode Island man's world record-breaking pumpkin"

item.title: Saturday 4 PM Update, Oct 17
item.description:
The Saturday four o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 17, 2026: President Trump rallies in Kentucky, air traffic controllers get a raise tied to new rules, France's nationwide protests turn violent and the historic Limoges town hall burns, Hurricane Trudy skirts Mexico's Pacific coast, Replit's CEO and Anthropic insiders disagree over their partnership, Google's lab-running A.I. agents, Anthropic's Code Review, the OpenCode key breach and urgent Drupal patches, your X feed with a big college football upset, a lobster study and events around York and the Seacoast, and two young sisters who play piano for people living with dementia. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Saturday 1 PM Update, Oct 17
item.description:

Ilhan Omar's lawyers push back on the search of her home, nationwide early-voting rallies, masked settlers attack European diplomats in the West Bank, Egypt's president seeks authority to help defend Saudi Arabia, a green light for the pope's Latin America trip, France and Germany's deal to soften Europe's 2035 car rules, a Honda redo recall, Anthropic's draft A.I. safety bill and its critics, a supply-chain attack on Microsoft 365 through ConnectWise, your X feed, a Sunday on the Seacoast, and a blind spaniel named Hero who learned to see with his nose. item.title: Saturday 10 AM Update, Oct 17
item.description:
